features.name: Academic Attainment
features.description: Captures the highest relevant formal academic preparation or degree level presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Agentic Systems Design
features.description: Captures direct experience designing agent-based systems, including autonomy boundaries, controls, orchestration, permissions, or auditability.

levels.descriptor: No direct agentic-system design described.
Mentions agents, automation, or multi-step workflows only in broad terms.
Clear experience pairing agents with back-end services or constraints.
Sophisticated description of agent autonomy plus guardrails such as permissions, auditing, bounded actions, or explicit control planes.

features.name: Algorithmic Fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI Production Experience
features.description: Captures the depth of real, shipped AI or LLM experience, especially with reliability, evaluation, or failure-mode handling in production.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer Enablement Mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant frames security engineering as helping developers through usable defaults, low-friction tooling, and empathy for internal users.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Evidence Specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter supports claims with specific examples, mechanisms, scope, or named artifacts rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists qualities or interests with little supporting evidence.
Includes a few examples but limited detail on ownership or effect.
Gives concrete examples of work with enough detail to make the claims credible.
Repeatedly ties claims to specific actions and clear outcomes or impact.

features.name: Formal Security Credentials
features.description: Captures the strength of formal third-party security certifications or other explicit external validation of security skill.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: Go Depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-relevant Go appears in the applicant's recent engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Does not provide meaningful evidence of Go use.
Mentions some Go exposure but not as a core language.
Presents Go as a major working language in production.
Presents Go as the principal or dominant language across core services.

features.name: Impact Articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter states the operational results, measurable outcomes, or effects of the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists interests or responsibilities with no clear outcomes.
Provides background counts but little evidence of what changed because of the work.
Shows at least one clear result or before-and-after effect.
Shows concrete, vivid, or measured outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to evaluate.

features.name: Narrative Cohesion
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a coherent, well-structured story or thesis rather than reading like a disconnected checklist.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative Distinctiveness
features.description: Captures how memorable, distinctive, and individually voiced the letter feels as a piece of writing.

levels.descriptor: Highly formulaic prose with little individual voice.
Competent but generic prose with only limited individuality.
Includes a memorable framing device, belief, or personal thesis.
Sustains a distinctive, authentic voice throughout while still serving the application's purpose.

features.name: Offensive Security Practice
features.description: Captures whether the applicant maintains ongoing attacker-oriented security practice outside ordinary product-engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-Source Stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for contributing to, fixing, or maintaining public codebases used beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or one-off fixes to dependencies.
Describes regular contribution or maintenance responsibility.
Shows stewardship of an actively used project or community, including review and release responsibility.

features.name: Personal Project Ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, seriousness, and follow-through of self-directed projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform Leverage Orientation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant is motivated by foundational or platform work whose impact compounds across many teams, products, or services.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production Delivery Track Record
features.description: Captures the breadth and depth of hands-on experience launching, maintaining, testing, and owning real production systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Professional Tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: Less than 2 years of clearly relevant experience, or tenure is not stated.
About 2 to 3 years of relevant experience; clears the minimum but is still early-career for this role.
About 4 to 5 years of relevant experience; solid mid-level tenure.
6 or more years of relevant experience; deep tenure for this opening.

features.name: Python Depth
features.description: Captures how central, substantial, and production-grade Python appears in the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: No Python experience is mentioned.
Mentions Python briefly or only as light scripting.
Describes regular Python use for tooling, automation, or services.
Shows deep Python ownership across production services or critical internal tooling.

features.name: Reliability and Maintainer Mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant emphasizes maintainability, failure modes, testing, rigor, and long-term operational responsibility.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Requirement Mapping
features.description: Captures how explicitly the letter maps the applicant's background to the posting's stated responsibilities, qualifications, or team needs.

levels.descriptor: The fit is vague and the reader must infer most of the relevance.
Some relevant matches are stated, but the mapping to the posting is incomplete or indirect.
Clearly connects several experiences to the role's stated needs.
Makes the match easy to verify, systematically covering most of the key qualifications or responsibilities.

features.name: Role-Specific Motivation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter explains why this exact role is an appealing and meaningful next step for the applicant.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in the company or job title with little role-specific reasoning.
Shows some relevant interest, but the motivation remains broad or interchangeable.
Clearly ties motivation to security engineering, developer enablement, or backend tooling.
Gives nuanced and convincing motivation tightly tied to this team's charter and responsibilities.

features.name: Security Assessment Practice
features.description: Captures the depth of hands-on experience reviewing systems for security issues and validating remediation, rather than merely expressing interest in security.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security Automation Mission Understanding
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands this job as scaling security work through automation and positions the applicant against that specific mission.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific framing beyond wanting security impact.
Shows general interest in secure defaults or automation, but not a sharp view of the problem.
Clearly frames security tooling as a way to scale review, response, or manual workload.
Frames the problem sharply in terms of scarce expert attention, organization-wide signal handling, variant analysis, or systems-level leverage.

features.name: Security Engineering Philosophy
features.description: Captures the maturity and thoughtfulness of the applicant's stated view of security engineering beyond generic interest or adjacency to security work.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability Workflow Automation
features.description: Captures direct ownership of tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related handling workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing Polish
features.description: Captures how mechanically polished, carefully proofread, and free of distracting spelling, grammar, or typographical errors the letter is.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Catch-all for smaller recurring constructs that do not cleanly fit the larger canonical criteria, including language breadth, collaboration posture, ownership seniority, and hybrid external-security-commitment signals.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.
